chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyād and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, all together from al-Ḥasan ibn al-ʿAbbās ibn al-Ḥarīsh, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī (عليه السلام), who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: While my father (عليه السلام) was performing tawaf around the Kaʿbah, suddenly a man wrapped in a turban, who had been assigned to him, interrupted his seven circuits until he brought him into a house beside al-Ṣafā. Then he sent for me, and we were three.

He said: Welcome, O son of the Messenger of Allah. Then he placed his hand on my head and said: May Allah bless you, O trustee of Allah after his forefathers. O Abā Jaʿfar, if you wish, then inform me; and if you wish, I shall inform you; and if you wish, ask me; and if you wish, I shall ask you; and if you wish, affirm me truthful; and if you wish, I shall affirm you truthful. He said: I desire all of that. He said: Then beware that your tongue should speak during my questioning with a matter while you conceal for me other than it. He said: Only one in whose heart are two knowledges does that, with one of them opposing the other; and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has refused that there be for Him any knowledge in which there is contradiction.

He said: This is my question, and you have explained part of it. Inform me about this knowledge in which there is no contradiction: who knows it? He said: As for the totality of knowledge, it is with Allah, majestic is His mention; and as for that from it which the servants cannot do without, it is with the awṣiyāʾ.

He said: So the man opened his head-wrap, sat upright, his face lit up, and he said: This is what I wanted, and for it I came. You claim that the knowledge in which there is no contradiction is with the awṣiyāʾ; so how do they know it? He said: Just as the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) used to know it, except that they do not see what the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) used to see, because he was a Prophet and they are spoken to, and because he used to go in delegation to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and hear the revelation, while they do not hear.

He said: You have spoken the truth, O son of the Messenger of Allah. I shall bring you a difficult question. Inform me about this knowledge: why is it that it does not appear as it used to appear with the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)? He said: My father (عليه السلام) smiled and said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has refused to disclose His knowledge except to one tested for faith in it, just as He decreed for the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) that he endure the harm of his people and not struggle against them except by His command.
How much concealment he maintained until it was said to him: “So proclaim openly what you are commanded, and turn away from the polytheists.”
And by Allah, if he had proclaimed openly before that, he would have been safe, but he only looked to obedience and feared dissension, and for that reason he withheld.

So I would wish that your eye might be with the Mahdī of this community, while the angels, with the swords of the family of Dāwūd, are between the heaven and the earth, punishing the souls of the disbelievers from among the dead and joining to them the souls of their likes from among the living. Then he brought out a sword and said: Here, indeed this is from them.

He said: So my father said: Yes, by the One who chose Muḥammad over mankind. He said: Then the man restored his turban-wrap and said: I am Ilyās. I did not ask you about your matter while I was ignorant of it; rather, I wished that this discourse should be a source of strength for your companions. And I shall inform you of a verse which you know; if they dispute by it, they will prevail. He said: So my father said to him: If you wish, I shall inform you of it. He said: I do wish.

He said: If our Shiʿah say to those who oppose us: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says to His Messenger (صلى الله عليه وآله): “Indeed We sent it down on the Night of al-Qadr,” to the end of it—then did the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) know any knowledge that he did not know on that night, or did Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) bring it to him at another time? Then they will say: No.

Then say to them: Was it necessary for everything he knew to be made manifest? They will say: No. Then say to them: Was there any contradiction in what the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) manifested of the knowledge of Allah, mighty is His mention? If they say: No, then say to them: So whoever judges by a judgment of Allah in which there is contradiction—has he opposed the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)? They will say: Yes. But if they say: No, then they have contradicted their first statement.
Then say to them: “None knows its interpretation except Allah and those firmly rooted in knowledge.”

If they say: Who are those firmly rooted in knowledge? then say: Those in whose knowledge there is no contradiction. If they say: Who is that? then say: The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was the possessor of that—so did he convey it or not? If they say: He did convey it, then say: Did he die (صلى الله عليه وآله) while the khalifah after him knew a knowledge in which there is no contradiction? If they say: No, then say: The successor of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) is divinely supported, and the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) appoints as successor only one who judges by his judgment, only one who is like him except for prophethood. And if the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) did not appoint anyone concerning his knowledge, then he would have neglected those in the loins of men who were to come after him.

And if they say to you: The knowledge of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was from the Qur’an, then say: “Ḥā Mīm. By the clear Book. Indeed We sent it down on a blessed night; indeed We are warners,” up to His saying: “Indeed We are senders.”

If they say to you: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends only to a prophet, then say: This wise affair which is differentiated therein—is it from the angels and the Spirit that descends from one heaven to another, or from heaven to earth? If they say: From heaven to heaven, then there is no one in heaven who turns back from obedience to disobedience. And if they say: From heaven to earth—then the people of the earth are the most in need among creation of that.

Then say: Is there not for them an unavoidable need for a master to whom they refer in judgment? If they say: The khalifah is their judge, then say: “Allah is the guardian of those who believe; He brings them out from darknesses into the light,” up to His saying: “abiding forever.”

By my life, there is neither on the earth nor in the heaven any friend of Allah, mighty is His mention, except that he is divinely supported; and whoever is supported does not err. And there is neither on the earth any enemy of Allah, mighty is His mention, except that he is forsaken; and whoever is forsaken does not reach correctness. Just as the affair must necessarily descend from heaven for the people of the earth to judge by it, likewise there must necessarily be a walī. If they say: We do not recognize this, then say to them: Say whatever you wish—Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has refused after Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وآله) to leave the servants without a hujjah over them.

Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: Then he paused, and said: Here, O son of the Messenger of Allah, is a subtle matter. What do you think if they say: The proof of Allah is the Qur’an? He said: Then I would say to them: The Qur’an is not one that speaks, commands, and forbids; rather, the Qur’an has people who command and forbid. And I would say: A calamity may befall some people of the earth which is not in the sunnah and the judgment in which there is no contradiction, and is not in the Qur’an. Allah, by His knowledge of that trial, has refused that it should appear on the earth while there would be in His judgment no repeller for it and no reliever for its people.

He said: Here is where you will prevail, O son of the Messenger of Allah. I bear witness that Allah, mighty is His mention, knew what would afflict creation of calamity on the earth or in themselves, in religion or other than it, so He placed the Qur’an as a guide. He said: Then the man said: Do you know, O son of the Messenger of Allah, what guide it is? Abū Jaʿfar (عليه السلام) said: Yes; in it are the general outlines of the prescribed limits, and their explanation is at the time of judgment. He said: Allah has refused that a servant be afflicted with a calamity in his religion, or in himself, or in his wealth, while there would not be upon His earth, from His judgment, one who judges correctly regarding that calamity.

He said: Then the man said: As for this matter, you have prevailed over them with a proof, unless your opponent fabricates against Allah and says: Allah, majestic is His mention, has no proof. But inform me about the interpretation of: “So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you, nor rejoice in what He has given you.”

He said: It is regarding Abū so-and-so and his companions—one part placed first and one part placed later: “So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you” from that with which ʿAlī (عليه السلام) was specially favored, “nor rejoice in what He has given you” of the tribulation that came upon you after the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله).
Then the man said: I bear witness that you are the possessors of the judgment in which there is no contradiction. Then the man stood and left, and I did not see him again.

key_terms.اخْتِلَافٌ: contradiction or divergence, negated from true divine knowledge and judgment
key_terms.الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ: those firmly rooted in knowledge, identified here through their possession of non-contradictory divine knowledge
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءِ: the divinely designated successors who possess the knowledge needed by the servants
key_terms.الْعِلْمِ: the divinely granted knowledge, especially that in which there is no contradiction
key_terms.حُجَّةَ: the divine proof or authority through whom Allah establishes guidance over the servants
key_terms.مَهْدِيِّ: the guided one from this Ummah associated here with the future manifestation of divine justice
key_terms.مُحَدَّثُونَ: those who are spoken to or inspired, describing the Imams without prophethood
key_terms.وَالٍ: a divinely appointed guardian or authority necessary for governing by what descends from heaven

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith use Laylat al-Qadr and Qur’anic verses to prove the continuing authority of the Imams after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a theological argument that the knowledge necessary for the guidance of creation remains with the divinely appointed awṣiyāʾ after the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It links the descent of divine command in Laylat al-Qadr to the ongoing need for a living hujjah and interprets Qur’anic verses to establish the authority of the Imams عليهم السلام. It also contains eschatological allusions to the Mahdi of this Ummah and emphasizes that Allah does not leave the servants without proof.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Abdu Abdullah and Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Al Hassan Bin Al Abbas Bin Al Harysh, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’farasws the 2nd who said, ‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘While myasws fatherasws was performing Tawaaf of the Kabah, when a man covered by a turban of his like an egg-shell, cut off hisasws seven (circuits) until he made himasws enter into a house by the side of Al-Safa. So heasws sent for measws, and we became three. So he said, ‘Welcome, O sonasws of Rasool-Allahsaww!’ Then he placed his hand upon myasws head and said, ‘May Allahazwj Bless youasws, O trustees of Allahazwj after hisasws forefathersasws! O Abu Ja’farasws! If youasws so desire, so inform me and if youasws so desire, so I shall inform youasws, and if youasws so desire, ask me, and if youasws so desire, I shall ask youasws, and if youasws so desire, ratify me, and if youasws so desire, I shall ratify youasws’. Heasws said: ‘All of that Iasws like’. He said, ‘So beware of speaking by your tongue during my questioning by a matter with something else in yourasws consciousness’. Heasws said: ‘But rather that is the one in whose heart are two knowledges, one of it opposing its counterpart, and that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Refused that there should be a Knowledge for Himazwj wherein is a differing’. He said, ‘This is my question, and you have explained part of it. Inform me about this knowledge which there is no differing in it. Who knows it?’ Heasws said: ‘But, the totality of the knowledge, so it is with Allahazwj, Majestic is Hisazwj Mention, and as for what is a must for the servants from it, so it is with the successorsasws’. Heasws said: ‘So the man opened up his turban and sat evenly (relaxed manner), and his face was cheerful, and he said, ‘This is what I wanted, and for it I came over. Youasws claim that knowledge is what there is no differing therein, from the knowledge with the succesorsasws, so how do they know it?’ Heasws said: ‘Just as how Rasool-Allahsaww used to know it except that theyasws are not seeing what Rasool-Allahsaww used to see, because hesaww was a Prophetsaww, and theyasws are Muhaddisoun, and it was so that heasws would be a delegate to Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic and hesaww would hear the Revelation, and theyasws are not hearing’. You speak the truth, O sonasws of Rasool-Allahsaww! I shall come to you with a difficult question. Inform me about this knowledge. What is the matter with it that it is not apparent (now) just as it was apparent with Rasool-Allahsaww?’ So myasws fatherasws smiled and said: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Refuses that anyone should have notification of Hisazwj Knowledg except for the one examined for the Eman with it, just as Heazwj Ordained upon Rasool-Allahsaww that hesaww be patient upon the harm of hissaww people, and hesaww should not fight against them except by Hisazwj Command. So how much from the secrets hesaww was secretive with until it was said to himsaww, ‘[15:94] Therefore declare openly what you are Commanded with and turn aside from the polytheists. And I swear by Allahazwj that had hesaww proclaimed openly before that, hesaww would (still) have been safe, but hesaww, rather, considered to be in the obedience and feared the differing (of people). Therefore, due to that, hesaww restrained. So, Iasws would love it if your eyes happen to be with the Mahdiasws of this community, and the Angels with the swords of the family of Dawoodas, between the sky and the earth, Punishing the souls of the disbelievers from the deceased and join with them the souls of their likes from the living ones’. Then heasws brought out a sword, then said: ‘Here, this is from those’. Heasws said: ‘So myasws fatherasws said: ‘Yes. By the Oneazwj Who Chose Muhammadsaww over (all) the human beings!’. So the man returned his turban and said, ‘I am Ilyasas. Ias did not ask youasws about yourasws matter and there was ignorance with me from it, apart from that Ias loved it that this Hadeeth takes place, as a strengthening for yourasws companions, and Ias shall inform you with a Verse youasws recognise it, if they were to debate with it, they would win’. So myasws fatherasws said to him: ‘If youas so desire, Iasws shall inform youas with it’. He said, ‘I do desire it’. Heasws said: ‘Ourasws Shias, if they were to be saying to the people is opposition to usasws that Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying to Hisazwj Rasoolsaww [97:1] We have indeed revealed this in the Night of Predestination – up to its end. So, did Rasool-Allahsaww know anything from the knowledge which hesaww did not know during that night, or Jibraeelas came with it during other than it? So if they would be saying, ‘No’, so say to them, ‘So was it inevitable from what hesaww knew that hesaww should manifest it?’ So they would be saying, ‘No’. So say to them, ‘So what there, regarding what Rasool-Allahsaww did manifest, from the Knowledge of Allahazwj, Mighty is Hisazwj Mention, any differing?’ So if they say, ‘No’, so say to them, ‘Therefore the one who judges by a Judgment of Allahazwj wherein is a differing, so has he opposed Rasool-Allahsaww?’ So they would be saying, ‘Yes’. So if they say, ‘No’, so they have broken their first speech. So say to them, ‘[3:7] but none knows its interpretation except Allah, and those who are firmly rooted in the Knowledge’. So if they say, ‘Who are the ones firmly rooted in the Knowledge?’ So say, ‘The ones in whose knowledge there is no differing’. So if they say, ‘So who is that?’ So say, ‘Rasool-Allahsaww was an owner of that. So did hesaww deliver or not?’ So if they say, ‘Hesaww did deliver’, so say, ‘Hesaww passed away and the Caliph from after himsaww had knowledge wherein there was no differing?’ So if they say, ‘No’, so say, ‘A Caliph of Rasool-Allahsaww is Assisted, and Rasool-Allahsaww would not leave behind anyone except the one who judged by hissaww judgment, and except one who would happen to be similar to himsaww except for the Prophet-hood, and if it was so that Rasool-Allahazwj did not leave anyone behind regarding hissaww knowledge, so hesaww would have wasted the ones who are in the loins of the men, from the ones who would be coming (to the world) after himsaww’. So if they say to you, ‘The knowledge of Rasool-Allahsaww was from the Quran’, so say, [44:1] Ha Mim! [44:2] I swear by the Clarifying Book [44:3] Surely We Revealed it on a Blessed Night surely We are ever Warning – up to Hisazwj Words [44:5] surely We are the Senders (of Messages)’. So if they say to you, ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic does not Send a Message except to a Prophetas, so say, ‘This 44:4] Therein every wise affair is made distinct, it is from the Angels and the Spirit who descend from a sky to a sky or from a sky to the earth?’ So if they say, ‘From a sky to a sky’, so there isn’t anyone in the sky who returns from obedience to disobedience. So if they say, ‘From sky to the earth’, and the people of the earth are more needy of the creatures to that. So say, ‘So is there a must for them to have a chief they would be going to for the judgments?’ So if they say, ‘So the Caliph, he is their judge’. So say, ‘[2:257] Allah is the Guardian of those who believe. He Extracts them from the darkness into the Light – up to Hisazwj Words in it they shall be abiding. By myasws life! There is neither in the sky nor in the earth, a Guardian of Allahazwj, Mighty is Hisazwj Mention, except that heasws is Assisted, and the one who is Assisted would not err, and there is neither in the sky nor in the earth, an enemy of Allahazwj, Mighty is Hisazwj Mention except that he is Abandoned, and the one who is Abandoned would not be correct (in his judgments). Just as it is inevitable for there to be a Revelation which descends from the sky for the people of the earth to be judged with, like that, it is inevitable for there to be a Guardianasws. So if they say, ‘We do not recognise this’. So say to them, ‘Say whatever you so like to. Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Refused that after Muhammadsaww Heazwj should leave the servants and there is no Divine Authority upon them’. Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Then heasws paused, so he (Ilyasas) said: ‘Over here, O sonasws of Rasool-Allahsaww, is a vague door. What is yourasws view if they were to say, ‘The Divine Authority is the Quran’?’ Heasws said: ‘Then Iasws would be saying to them: ‘The Quran is not with a speech, Ordering and Prohibiting, but for the Quran there are peopleasws who are ordering and prohibiting,’ and Iasws would be saying: ‘There would get presented to some people of the earth, a difficulty which is not in the Sunnah, and the judgment wherein there is no differing, and it isn’t in the Quran, Allahazwj refused that (situation to occur) for Hisazwj Knowledge, for that strife to appear in the earth and there is no refutation for it in Hisazwj Judgment, and a relief for its people’. So he (Ilyasas) said: ‘Over here youasws are winning, O sonasws of Rasool-Allahsaww! Ias testify that Allahazwj, Mighty is Hisazwj Mention had Known of what would be hitting the creatures from difficulties in the earth, or regarding themselves from the Religion, or something else, so Heazwj Placed the Quran as Evidence’. Heasws said: ‘So the man (Ilyasas) said: ‘Do youasws know, O sonasws of Rasool-Allahsaww the Evidence, what it is?’ Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘Yes, therein is the totality of the Legal Punishments, and its interpretation during the judgment’. So heas said: ‘Allahazwj Refuses that a servant be hit by a difficulty in his Religion, or regarding himself, or in his wealth, and there isn’t in Hisazwj earth from Hisazwj Judgment which can be judged with the correctness with regards to that very difficulty’. Heasws said: ‘So the man (Ilyasas) said: ‘But, in this door (subject matter), youasws would be winning with an argument except if they were to forge against Allahazwj in disputing youasws, so they would be saying, ‘There isn’t a Divine Authority for Allahazwj, Majestic is Hisazwj Mention’. But, inform meas about the interpretation of [57:23] So that you may not despair over what has escaped you from what Aliasws has been Specialised with, nor be happy at what He has Given you’. Heasws said: ‘(It is) regarding Abu so and so, and his companion. One who was foremost and one who was delayed (later one) [57:23] So that you may not despair over what has escaped you from what Aliasws has been Specialised with, nor be happy at what He has Given you, from the strife which appeared for you after Rasool-Allahsaww’. So the man (Ilyasas) said: ‘Ias testify that you Imamsasws are the owners of the wisdom wherein there is no differing’. Then the man stood up and went, and Iasws did not see him (again)’.
en.sarwar: al-Qadr, Destiny 97 In the Name of God, the Beneficent, the Merciful We revealed the Quran on the Night of Destiny ([97:1].

Would that you knew what the Night of Destiny is! [97:2]. (Worship) on the Night of Destiny is better than (worship) for a thousand months [97:3]. On this Night, the angels and the spirit descend by the permission of their Lord with His decree (to determine everyone’s destiny) [97:4]. This Night is all peace until the break of dawn [97:5].
